The cuts include the closure of the sports desk and bureaus in the Middle East and Ukraine, affecting correspondents reporting from conflict zones. 
Owner Jeff Bezos, who purchased the paper in 2013, has made no public comment on the layoffs, which follow controversy over his decision to block an endorsement of Kamala Harris in the 2024 election, leading to the cancellation of 200,000 subscriptions. 
The newspaper that helped bring down a president through its Watergate reporting in the 1970s now faces questions about its future as a legendary news brand.

Al Jazeera’s Mike Hanna reports from Washington, DC.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The New Start Treaty, which capped deployed nuclear warheads and allowed mutual site inspections, expired on 5 February. 
Russia had offered to extend the agreement for another year, maintaining limits on warheads and delivery systems, but says it received no response from the United States. 
President Donald Trump has indicated he wants China included in any future nuclear arms control deal, though Beijing has ruled out participation until its stockpile reaches parity with Washington and Moscow. 
With no informal extension in place and no new negotiations underway, the world is now without a legally binding nuclear arms control framework between the two largest nuclear powers for the first time in over 50 years.

Al Jazeera's Shihab Rattansi reports from Washington, DC.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The Syrian government is reasserting control in northeastern Syria after years of Kurdish-led SDF rule during the civil war.
Recent clashes were followed by a ceasefire and an agreement to integrate the SDF into state institutions.
Under the deal, Damascus will take control of oil and gas fields and detention centres holding ISIL prisoners.
Syrian security forces have entered Hasakah and Qamishli, positioning small convoys in strategic locations.
Day-to-day security on the streets remains with the Kurdish Asayish police.
Many Kurds remain uncertain about their future, fearing the loss of political and civil rights.
The government has pledged to protect those rights, including recognising Kurdish as a national language.

Al Jazeera's Teresa Bo reports from Qamishli, Syria.

description:
A limited number of Palestinians have been allowed to return to Gaza via the Rafah crossing after months of medical treatment abroad, highlighting stringent screening and prolonged delays. 

Rotana Al-Raqab and her mother, back after 11 months away, described belongings being confiscated and hours of questioning by Israeli authorities. 

Al Jazeera’s Ibrahim Al-Khalili reports from Khan Younis, Gaza.
